alt: Poster: Expiry-day margin rules for index derivatives per SEBI circular of 1 Oct 2024 - no calendar spread benefit on expiry day, extra 2% ELM on short options, premium collected upfront
text:
Expiry day carries its own margin rules, and they are easy to overlook.

SEBI's circular of 1 October 2024 (SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2024/132) on strengthening the equity index derivatives framework set three of them. Since 1 February 2025, the calendar spread margin benefit is not available on the day of expiry for contracts expiring that day. Since 20 November 2024, an additional extreme loss margin (ELM) of 2% applies to short options contracts expiring that day. And since 1 February 2025, upfront margin collection by members includes the net options premium payable at the client level.

The circular's stated aim is to curb undue intraday leverage and expiry-day risks. Calendar spread treatment for contracts expiring on other days is unchanged.

Our view: these rules raise the margin cost of holding short options positions into expiry. That is an interpretation of the mechanics, not a recommendation.

For practitioners: how has expiry-day margin treatment changed the way you or your clients size and manage positions into expiry?
